description: Modal frequencies of struck metal. Unlike tubes/voices, metal partials are INHARMONIC — not integer multiples — which is what makes metal sound metallic. To author, multiply each ratio by a chosen fundamental (Hz) and place a resonance there. Metal rings hard, so radii are high (narrow bandwidth).
source: Standard vibration theory: free-free & cantilever Euler-Bernoulli beams, flat circular plate modes (Chladni), and the canonical 'minor-third' tuned-bell partial set (Rossing, Fletcher & Rossing 'Physics of Musical Instruments').

q_guidance.note: Struck metal = very high Q (long ring) = narrow bandwidth = high radius. The Q axis tightens it further toward a pure ring.

morph_guidance: Metal morphs by (a) STRIKE/material — which partials dominate (level), or (b) swapping object. For the Hedz template: anchor the stable high partials, and let the lowest two partials CROSS (the fundamental and 2nd mode trade emphasis) for a 'struck -> ringing' migration. Q = damping -> pure ring.

objects.name: struck uniform bar, free-free (glockenspiel/uncut xylophone)
objects.note: the classic 'clang' — 2.76x first overtone is the metallic signature

objects.name: cantilever rod/tine, clamped one end (thumb-piano / chime / tuning-fork tine)
objects.note: huge gaps between partials -> pure, woody-metallic ping

objects.name: free flat circular plate (cymbal-ish / sheet / 'anvil' plate)
objects.note: dense, closely-packed inharmonic modes -> shimmery metallic wash

objects.name: tuned church bell (minor-third partial set)
objects.note: tierce at 1.2x (a minor third above prime) is what makes a bell sound bell-like and faintly sad

objects.name: gong / tam-tam (dense chaotic cluster)
objects.note: no clear pitch; very dense low-mid cluster that blooms upward when struck hard

morph_pairs.name: muted -> ringing bell
morph_pairs.motion: low partials (hum/prime) cross emphasis with the tierce/nominal as the strike opens up

morph_pairs.name: bar -> plate
morph_pairs.motion: sparse clang dissolves into a dense plate shimmer
